stem:
The diagram shows Rumi's four-sided card, tilted on the page. Every side is $4\,\mathrm{cm}$, and every corner is $90^\circ$.

Which claim correctly names the figure?

options.text: A square, because all sides are equal and all angles are $90^\circ$, even though the card is tilted.
A rectangle only, because any four-sided shape with right angles is called a rectangle.
A square, because the four sides are equal.
Not a square, because tilting the card is what changes its side lengths and angles.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal sides and four right angles make a square, tilt or not. Calling it only a rectangle substitutes the weaker label. Equal sides alone omit the angle condition. Saying tilt changes the measures reverses cause.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as a tilted square PQRS with equal 4 cm sides and a right-angle mark; stem refers to the diagram.
